note: Authored by reading Tafsir al-Tabari in English against the reader's modern translation. Each phrase carries the app's own words for that piece of the verse, a plain modern English line of my own, the Arabic of the piece, and the numbered paragraphs of the commentary that speak of it.

phrases.text: The Hour that strikes the hearts of people with its terror, the morning after which no night follows. The commentators say the word is one of the names of the day of resurrection.
The question is asked to magnify the weight of the Hour, so that the servants are struck with dread of it. How tremendous it is.

phrases.translation: And what will make you realize what the Striking Disaster is
phrases.text: What has made you know, O Muhammad, what the Striking Disaster is.

phrases.translation: ˹It is˺ the Day people will be like scattered moths
phrases.text: The word means the insect that falls into the fire and the lamp, and the scattered, the dispersed. Some said it is the swarm you have seen plunging into the fire, and some said it is a parable for a swarm of locusts crawling over one another.

phrases.translation: and the mountains will be like carded wool
phrases.text: And the word means wool of many colours. It is said that the mountains move over the earth while still keeping their shape, like dust.

phrases.translation: So as for those whose scale is heavy ˹with good deeds˺
phrases.text: His scales of good deeds are heavy. The word means the weight, and Mujahid said there is no scale, it is only a likeness set forth.

phrases.translation: they will be in a life of bliss
phrases.text: In a life that he finds pleasing, in the Garden.

phrases.translation: And as for those whose scale is light
phrases.text: His scale of good deeds turns out light, and his refuge and dwelling place is the Hawiya, into which he falls head first into the Fire.

phrases.translation: their home will be the abyss
phrases.text: The Fire is his mother and his dwelling place, for he has no other. Tabari says the Fire is called his mother only because it has become his home, as a woman gives shelter to her child, and he gives the saying the Arabs used when a man fell into a grave matter.

phrases.translation: And what will make you realize what that is
phrases.text: What, O Muhammad, has made you know what al-Hawiya is.
The word means the fire that is heated by the fuel kindled upon it.
